newsitem.title: UK: Policeman injured in Northern Ireland blast.
newsitem.headline: Policeman injured in Northern Ireland blast.

text.p: A policeman was slightly injured in an explosion on Sunday night as a security force patrol passed through a Northern Ireland village, police said on Monday.
The area around the blast in Pomeroy, about 40 miles (65 km) west of Belfast, was sealed off and several homes were evacuated.
Police did not give a reason for the explosion which followed two bomb attacks last week on police vehicles in the British-ruled province. Investigations would continue on Monday, they said.

The Irish Republican Army (IRA), seeking to end British rule, has bombed security targets in Northern Ireland several times a week this year to back its demand that its political wing Sinn Fein be invited to Belfast peace talks.

Sinn Fein leader Gerry Adams, speaking exactly a year after the IRA ended a ceasefire, urged Prime Minister John Major on Sunday to let his party back into peace talks before the forthcoming British general election.
The government insisted its terms for Sinn Fein to attend the talks -- an unequivocal IRA ceasefire -- had not changed but conceded a meeting might still prove possible.
"Any meeting before that would not be totally ruled out but would depend on the situation on the ground," said a spokesman for the government's Northern Ireland Office.
If attacks such as those on security forces in Northern Ireland in recent weeks continued, no meeting would be agreed before the election, which must be held by May 22.

A huge bomb blast that killed two men at London's Canary Wharf business complex on February 9 last year heralded the IRA's return to war and threw the Anglo-Irish peace process for Northern Ireland into chaos.
